e-7418.knowledge_point: Computing the Expected Value of a Scaled Random Variable
e-7418.problem:
A random variable $X$ has the probability distribution given below.

| $x$ | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ | $4$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $\dfrac{1}{5}$ | $\dfrac{1}{10}$ | $\dfrac{3}{10}$ | $\dfrac{3}{10}$ | $\dfrac{1}{10}$ |

Calculate $\textrm E\left[\dfrac{1}{4}X\right].$
e-7418.worked_solution:
First, let's find $\textrm E[X].$ 

The expected value of a discrete random variable $X$ with probability mass function $f(x)$ and sample space $S$ is given by

$$
\textrm E[X] = \sum\limits_{x \in S} x \cdot f(x).
$$

Summing up the products of each value of $X$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & ={\sum }_{x\in S}x\cdot f(x) \\  & =0\cdot \frac{1}{5}+1\cdot \frac{1}{10}+2\cdot \frac{3}{10}+3\cdot \frac{3}{10}+4\cdot \frac{1}{10} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[\frac{1}{4}X] & =\text{E}[\frac{1}{4}X] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\text{E}[X] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot 2 \\  & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

e-9130.knowledge_point: Computing the Expected Value of a Transformed Random Variable
e-9130.worked_solution:
For any constants $a$ and $b$ and any random variable $X,$ we have

$$
\textrm E[aX+b] = a \textrm E[X]+b.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[1-4X] & =\text{E}[-4X+1] \\  & =-4\text{E}[X]+1 \\  & =-4(\frac{1}{2})+1 \\  & =-2+1 \\  & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:
First, let's find $\text{E}[X].$ 

The expected value of a discrete random variable $X$ with probability mass function $f(x)$ and sample space $S$ is given by

$$
\text{E}[X]={\sum }_{x\in S}x\cdot f(x).
$$

Summing up the products of each value of $X$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & ={\sum }_{x\in S}x\cdot f(x) \\  & =0\cdot 0.35+1\cdot 0.15+2\cdot 0.15+3\cdot 0.1+4\cdot 0.25 \\  & =1.75.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[-2X] & =-2\text{E}[X] \\  & =-2\cdot 1.75 \\  & =-3.5.\end{aligned}

The expected value of a discrete random variable $X$ with probability mass function $f(x)$ and sample space $S$ is given by

$$
\text{E}[X]={\sum }_{x\in S}x\cdot f(x).

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & ={\sum }_{x\in S}x\cdot f(x) \\  & =0\cdot 0.1+1\cdot 0.2+2\cdot 0.3+3\cdot 0.3+4\cdot 0.1 \\  & =2.1.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[3X] & =3\text{E}[X] \\  & =3\cdot 2.1 \\  & =6.3.\end{aligned}
$$
